#22126. Efficient Quantum Monte Carlo through Cluster Expansions

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1m • 📖 Standard (211 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Arxiv ↗ Open Full Page

Efficient Quantum Monte Carlo through Cluster Expansions

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (211 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

Recent findings suggest that arXiv:2610.03893v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The sign problem remains a major obstacle to extending the success of Monte Carlo methods to generic quantum many-body systems. A powerful alternative relies on cluster expansions, which provide convergent representations of free energies and related quantities, with applications ranging from tensor network contractions to quantum dynamics and circuits. Within their convergence regime, these expansions often yield deterministic polynomial-time algorithms. However, such methods require exhaustive enumeration of connected clusters, leading to a computational overhead of $(N\varepsilon^{-1})^{\mathcal{O}(\log\Delta)}$, where $N$ is the system size, $\varepsilon$ the desired precision, and $\Delta$ the interaction-graph degree. This becomes particularly severe in long-range systems, where $\Delta\equiv N$, resulting in quasi-polynomial runtimes. Here, we introduce a Markov chain algorithm that samples cluster expansions directly in the space of connected clusters, replacing deterministic enumeration by Monte Carlo sampling. Because sampling occurs in an abstract cluster space rather than a physical configuration space, the conventional exponential sign problem is absent within the convergence regime. For general polymer models, we establish an FPRAS with runtime $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(N^4\varepsilon^{-3})$. For quantum partition functions at temperatures $\beta\leq\beta_{\mathrm{sampling}}\equiv\mathcal{O}(1)$, this improves to $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(N^{3+1/D}\varepsilon^{-3})$, where $D$ is the lattice dimension. The framework applies to long-range quantum systems with interactions $\propto1/r^\alpha$, including $2$-local models with $\alpha>2D$.

#22102. A depolarizing choir sings in Gaussian harmony

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1m • 📖 Standard (158 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Arxiv ↗ Open Full Page

A depolarizing choir sings in Gaussian harmony

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (158 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

arXiv:2609.39747v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the noise threshold for positive quantum capacity for the qubit depolarizing channel. We explore analytically the action of the qubit depolarizing channel on the symmetric subspaces of the input qubits, in the limit of asymptotically many uses of the channel. We observe the emergence of a bosonic Gaussian channel. Furthermore, the codes previously developed for the depolarizing channel can be translated to codes for the emergent Gaussian channel, and it is easier to further optimize these codes for the simpler emergent Gaussian channel. Translating these codes back to the depolarizing channel leads to extremely good input states for the coherent information of the depolarizing channel producing new lower bounds on the noise threshold for positive capacity. In addition to improved lower bounds on the threshold, this newly found link between depolarizing noise and Gaussian channels offers a novel perspective contributing to our understanding of these symmetric codes.

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1m • 📖 Standard (212 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Arxiv ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Nonequilibrium energy transport and fluctuations in two-photon-driven nonlinear quantum optical systems

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (212 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

It has been revealed that arXiv:2609.23651v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Understanding nonequilibrium transport and fluctuations under a parametric drive in nonlinear quantum optical systems is challenging. Here, we formulate a driven quantum master equation in the rotating frame combined with full counting statistics, retaining the drive-induced frequency shifts in the system-reservoir interactions and providing a unified description of drive-assisted incoherent transitions based on the rotated system dressed-basis. Applied to a Kerr resonator and a nonlinear Jaynes-Cummings model, the approach reveals pronounced multiphoton-resonant enhancement of the drive input energy current, with significant high peaks under two-photon driving compared to the single-photon case. The two-photon resonance relations are analytically obtained. Resonance structure in the nonlinear Jaynes-Cummings model nonlinearly relies on qubit-photon couplings, with additional dressed-state branches. A low-energy-state approximation attributes the resonant current enhancement to dressed-state hybridization and efficient activation of incoherent energy exchange processes. Beyond the average current, two-photon-driving induced energy exchange picture near resonance also substantially modifies the second-order current fluctuation and higher-order current cumulant, while increasing the time-normalized signal-to-noise ratio. Adding two-photon loss introduces extra incoherent photon-pair exchange pathways and further reshapes the current and its fluctuations. We hope these results may deepen interpretation of photon driving and quantum dissipation cooperatively governing nonequilibrium energy transport and fluctuations.

Industry News: Exact Replica-Sector Hierarchy of Multi-Resolvent Spectral-Weight Fluctuations in Random Free Fermions

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (209 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish

Industry observers note that arXiv:2609.17037v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The one-point ETH envelope fixes the smooth part of a spectral density but not how the spectral weight of an eigenstate is distributed across channels; its higher-order correlations are joint fluctuations of those weights and are carried by connected products of channel resolvents. In random free fermions every channel overlap is a squared Slater minor of a Haar-orthogonal one-body eigenvector matrix, and the multi-resolvent hierarchy has an exact microscopic realization there. The $r$-resolvent moment admits a decomposition into finitely many overlap sectors whose values are fixed by the channel and eigenstate overlap patterns and whose weights are exact finite-$N$ orthogonal Weingarten functions: the sector theorem holds at arbitrary finite multiplicity, it is realized in full at $r=3$ ($k=2,3,4$) and through exact sector slices at $r=4,5$, and the sector moments lift to connected resolvent cumulants and to the irreducible Feshbach self-energy vertices, whose deep plane begins at the order $z^{-(3r-2)}$. At $r=2$ this structure reproduces and completes an exact benchmark in which a flat envelope coexists with a non-Porter--Thomas intensity hierarchy and closes the two-resolvent covariance, and under interaction it separates into a deep plane fixed by Hamiltonian channel moments and a bulk that requires eigenstate-resolved information.

We extend the analysis to tight-binding chains subject to uniform on-site phase damping. In the phasedamped case, we find that a Gaussian approximation for the quantum characteristic functions predicts current fluctuations with good accuracy.

General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Arxiv ↗ Open Full Page

Proof-of-principle long-distance Sagnac twin-field quantum key distribution network

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (182 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

Industry observers note that arXiv:2609.04447v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Twin-field (TF) quantum key distribution (QKD) offers a promising approach to long-distance QKD networks due to its superior performance over large channel losses. Due to specialized hardware requirements, nearly all long-distance TFQKD demonstrations have only two people exchanging keys, rather than a network with three or more users. In this work, we experimentally demonstrate a proof-of-principle three-user-pair Sagnac TFQKD network spanning 127-km using single-photon avalanche detectors without any active phase stabilization or postcompensation. We implement efficient procedures for maintaining polarization stability and circumventing Rayleigh backscattering noise to achieve a stable Sagnac interference visibility of $93\pm1$ % over one hour. Using measured data for the signal basis and simulated data for the decoy basis, an asymptotic secure key rate of $1.398\times10^{-5}$ bits per pulse is achieved over an asymmetric communication channel with 102-km fiber and 45-dB overall loss. To our knowledge, this is the first TFQKD network without active phase stabilization or postcompensation achieved over long fibers. Our results represent a highly practical and cost-effective approach to long-distance QKD networks.

📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Arxiv ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Exact Matching-Polynomial Solution of the Periodic Baxter-Fendley $Z_N$ Clock Chain

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (168 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

Recent findings suggest that arXiv:2608.18633v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The periodic-boundary non-Hermitian Baxter-Fendley $Z_N$ chain does not have the same free-parafermionic structure as the open-boundary chain. We construct a matching polynomial for the corresponding cycle of its cyclic Weyl algebra. Its coefficients form conserved quantities containing the periodic Hamiltonian, while the matching polynomial itself realizes a Yang-Baxter transfer matrix. Root-of-unity fusion gives a second matching-polynomial closure and a system of spectral equations in each charge sector. The normalized energy resultant of these equations coincides with the charge-sector characteristic polynomial, yielding the complete finite-size energy spectrum with algebraic multiplicity. For positive reflection-symmetric chains, we prove that the periodic-boundary ground state is the unique analytic continuation of the open-boundary ground state. This yields an efficient large-size ground-state algorithm without enumerating the full spectrum. For the homogeneous three-state chain, seam-response asymptotics and finite-size ground-state calculations support two reciprocal candidate critical couplings distinct from the self-dual point, while the full periodic phase diagram is left for future work.

#22030. Optimal Dynamic Cooling of Multiple Qubits

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1m • 📖 Standard (236 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Arxiv ↗ Open Full Page

Optimal Dynamic Cooling of Multiple Qubits

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (236 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

Sources indicate that arXiv:2607.23641v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We solve the closed-system problem of cooling $M$ qubits, selected from $N$ identical thermal qubits, to the lowest common local temperature allowed by unitarity. The optimal protocol consists of two conceptually distinct steps. First, a passive rearrangement assigns the largest eigenvalues of the initial state to target sectors of lowest Hamming weight, thereby minimizing the total target energy. Second, a target-only complex-Hadamard transformation within each fixed-Hamming-weight subspace equalizes the one-qubit target marginals without changing any target-sector probability or the total energy. Consequently, imposing a common local temperature costs neither cooling depth nor additional work: the constrained optimum coincides with the unconstrained passive minimum for every $N>M$ and every initial temperature. The complex-Hadamard correction may nevertheless be costly at the circuit level. We therefore derive an exact arithmetic criterion for when the same optimum can be attained by a temperature-independent computational-basis permutation alone, and exhaustively classify the resulting finite-size islands of feasibility for $M+2\leq N\leq 128$. At isolated temperatures, further optimal permutations can arise through numerical cancellations between different thermal eigenvalue shells. These alternative realizations may reduce implementation complexity, but they cannot improve the cooling curve already attained by the universal protocol. We also derive the exact cooling curve, prove that at least two ancillary qubits are necessary and sufficient for nontrivial cooling, and show that joint many-target cooling can strictly outperform parallel single-target strategies.

Sources indicate that arXiv:2607.09660v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate Unruh-DeWitt detectors coupled to composite observables of a quantum scalar field, including quadratic coupling to the field momentum and coupling to the local energy density. We develop a distributional framework for evaluating the corresponding detector response functions and apply it to detectors crossing the Rindler firewall. While we recover the finite response of the derivative-coupling model, we show that quadratic momentum coupling leads to products of distributions that do not admit a canonical, regulator-independent definition in the sharp-firewall idealization. The vacuum correspondence between the local energy-density and quadratic momentum responses motivates the conjecture that analogous difficulties may arise for energy-density coupling in the sharp firewall model. Within the sharp, pointlike composite-coupling model considered here, our analysis further suggests that these pathologies originate from the discontinuous severing of correlations across the Rindler horizon.

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (148 words, ⚡ Quick Read) | Source: Arxiv

Recent findings suggest that arXiv:2607.06932v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In multiphoton blockade, drive-induced excitations are not necessarily fully converted into cavity photons, leaving unwanted lower-photon-number contributions that degrade source purity. This motivates a source-oriented component-selection strategy, in which the internal composition of the resonant two-excitation state is tailored to favor the component associated with the desired quantum-light output. In a cavity-coupled two-atom system, by engineering the resonant-state composition and controlling the interference between excitation pathways, we suppress both single- and three-photon backgrounds at matched two-photon populations, although a residual single-photon contribution remains. This residual background originates from a structural tradeoff between the photonic character of the target state and the spectral anharmonicity required for photon-number selectivity. Furthermore, selecting the double-atomic-excitation component at another operating point enables the generation of strongly correlated fluorescence photon pairs, demonstrating two distinct two-photon sources within the same physical platform.

#22013. Industry News: Overcoming configuration bottleneck: Modular pathways to stable semiconductor spin-qubit arrays

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1m • 📖 Standard (187 w)
📖 Baca
Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Arxiv ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: Overcoming configuration bottleneck: Modular pathways to stable semiconductor spin-qubit arrays

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (187 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

arXiv:2606.30883v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Over the past decade, semiconductor spin qubits have progressed from few-qubit demonstrations toward larger-scale devices fabricated in increasingly reproducible academic and industrial processes. This progress marks an inflection point: the central challenge is no longer to demonstrate high-fidelity operation in carefully tuned devices but to discover, verify, and maintain stable operating conditions reliably across many interdependent controls, varied device geometries, and disparate material platforms. In this Perspective, we frame spin-qubit operation as a modular automation problem. We decompose the workflow into five modules: bootstrapping from minimal prior information, configuration tuning, virtualization of physical gates into effective control axes, qubit-level tuning, and an operation layer with drift-aware maintenance. Using recent demonstrations from our work and the broader community, we argue that scalability will depend on explicit interfaces between modules, standardized intermediate data products, and workflow-level metrics such as throughput, success probability, stability time, recovery time, and robustness. We close by outlining the infrastructure needed to move beyond isolated tuning demonstrations toward sustained operation: qubit-performance-aware feedback, reusable software and benchmark tasks, and tight collaboration among experimental, theoretical, and software efforts.

#22008. BEVCast: Path-Adaptive BEV for Efficient End-to-End Autonomous Driving

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1m • 📖 Standard (249 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Arxiv ↗ Open Full Page

BEVCast: Path-Adaptive BEV for Efficient End-to-End Autonomous Driving

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (249 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

arXiv:2611.08631v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Camera-based driving models build a dense bird's-eye-view (BEV) grid and spend the same computation on every cell of it, although the vehicle crosses only a few of those cells within the planning horizon. We present BEVCast, a two-stage BEV whose resolution adapts to the predicted driving path. A coarse pass encodes the whole scene on a grid of 4.096 m cells. A heat head trained on the recorded path assigns a heat to every coarse cell and the cells with the highest heat are refined into 1.024 m cells under a fixed budget. The remaining cells keep their coarse resolution, so the trajectory head reads a mixed-resolution BEV that still covers the entire scene and needs neither an HD map nor a navigation command. Against a full grid of 1.024 m cells with the same architecture and training recipe, BEVCast at a 10% refinement budget encodes 28% of the BEV queries and needs 66% of the BEV encoder time at batch size 1. On nuScenes its mean displacement error is 1.078 m against 1.149 m and its drivable area violation rate is 1.46% against 2.29%. On NAVSIM navtest its mean displacement error is 0.577 m against 0.598 m and its extended predictive driver model score is 82.51 against 81.28. Next to published planners BEVCast reaches a comparable error on both benchmarks without a navigation command. The resolution of a driving BEV can therefore follow the task instead of the grid.

#22002. Consensus Within, Competition Between: Decentralized LLM Teams for Perimeter Defense

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1m • 📖 Standard (228 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Arxiv ↗ Open Full Page

Consensus Within, Competition Between: Decentralized LLM Teams for Perimeter Defense

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (228 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

arXiv:2610.41044v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The use of large language models (LLMs) to coordinate multi-agent teams raises a fundamental architectural question: whether task allocation should be centralized in a single LLM controller or distributed across autonomous LLM agents, particularly when communication is unreliable. In a deliberately simplified perimeter-defense simulation against LLM-controlled intruders, we compared a central commander, an auction-based consensus team and independent agents under five network conditions. Breach rates were 15% for the consensus team, 32% for the commander and 29% for independent agents. Burst message loss, falsified reports and limited radio range raised the commander's breach rate by 10 to 18 percentage points (pp), whereas the consensus team's changed by at most 5. In the consensus team, giving a low-cost LLM more authority over the bid computation raised its breach rate by 38 pp. With birds and civilian drones in airspace, we added an image for each to the input text state. Only the near-frontier model treated them apart from intruders. Intruders disguised as existing taxidermy bird drones were mistaken for birds by both low-cost and near-frontier LLMs, being dropped from pursuit in 59-61% of near-frontier decisions (1-16% before). However, a one-sentence forewarning in the prompt lowered it to 0-25%. We find that the LLM team with a dedicated external conflict-resolution protocol had the fewest breaches. The code is available at https://github.com/the-kas-lab/consensus-within-competition-between.

Given an energy shift $\omega$, QIPI prepares the target excited state by iteratively applying an approximation of the shifted inverse Hamiltonian $(H-\omega I)^{-1}$ to a trial state. Prior quantum inverse power approaches typically relied on Fourier decompositions of the inverse Hamiltonian, with numerical quadrature used to reconstruct the transformation, but such methods are highly sensitive to hyperparameter choices and have been observed to be numerically unstable, effectively restricting their use to ground-state preparation. Numerical simulations for molecular Hamiltonians of H$_2$, LiH, and BeH$_2$ show improved convergence and enhanced access to higher excited states relative to other quantum power methods. Assuming standard oracle access to the Hamiltonian, we further provide logical resource estimates in fault-tolerant settings in terms of T gate counts, and conclude that QIPI can achieve high target state amplification with modest polynomial degrees, thereby making it a promising candidate for scalable excited-state preparation in fault-tolerant quantum chemistry applications.

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (277 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

📖 0% read

arXiv:2610.26979v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Latent world models let an agent blueprint in latent space. The planner searches for an action sequence that minimizes a cost, and that cost is often the $\ell_2$ distance between the predicted terminal latent and the goal latent. The latent, however, is partly noise: the regularizer that prevents collapse during world model training promotes variance in the directions carrying no signal. We show that the same regularizer also supplies the structure to prune that noise in the latent. SIGReg drives the latent marginal to a standard Gaussian at every step, and assuming further that the latent sequence is a Gauss-Markov process, the transition is linear with its covariance pinned by the map itself, $z' \mid z \sim N(Az,\, I - AA^\top)$. Fitting the state dynamics $A$ therefore yields the covariance at no additional cost, and in its eigenbasis each latent direction carries its own uncertainty. Furthermore, constraining $A$ to be a normal matrix fixes that basis across timesteps, so one eigenbasis measures the uncertainty over an arbitrary number of steps and serves as a stable basis to compute the planning cost on. We then restrict the $\ell_2$ cost to the $k$-dimensional subspace the state dynamics carry forward with the least uncertainty. The correction is post hoc: the encoder, the predictor, the rollout, and the planner are all left untouched, and only a single constrained matrix, $A$, is fit. We evaluate across six environments and show large gains on the 2D navigation tasks, TwoRoom and PointMaze, raising success rate over the plain $\ell_2$ cost by up to $+54.7$ points under a harder planning setting. Code is available at https://github.com/yjang43/lp2.

Industry observers note that arXiv:2610.24122v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) requires long-horizon instruction-consistent planning and short-horizon path planning grounded in the currently observed geometry. Anticipating how future observations evolve along the instructed route provides predictive guidance beyond the current field of view, motivating video-action models (VAMs) that learn representations of future visual states. However, many existing VAMs couple future visual prediction with action generation during inference, despite their distinct temporal requirements: instruction-conditioned route guidance can be reused across multiple control steps, whereas local trajectories must continuously adapt to fresh observations. To bridge this gap, we introduce HAVANA, a dual-system VAM that decouples predictive reasoning from reactive local planning. A slow system produces a compact language-conditioned latent blueprint from observation history, while a fast system combines the latest plan with the current observation to generate local trajectories. Their asynchronous execution enables rapid adaptation without repeated future prediction, and no future video is generated during inference. Experiments on OmniNavBench demonstrate state-of-the-art navigation performance over prior baselines, while zero-shot real-world deployments further show robust generalization to unseen environments.

Recent findings suggest that arXiv:2606.23392v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the domain of quantum communication, cryptographic protocols often require owners to have access to trusted qubit sources or detectors. Recently, it was shown that on an architecture called the Qline, several protocols can equivalently be performed by parties capable only of single-qubit rotations. In this work, we introduce two composably secure constructions that together show how in most quantum cryptographic protocols, parties traditionally required to perform trusted qubit preparation or measurement can delegate these tasks to an untrusted provider and instead rely on a trusted single-qubit rotation device. Our first construction implements single-qubit measurement and is universally applicable across any context. In contrast, our second construction, which addresses qubit preparation, relies on specific assumptions regarding the underlying protocol. We show, however, that these assumptions are inherently satisfied by the vast majority of common quantum cryptographic protocols. A notable consequence of our results is the formal validation of the Qline as a versatile architecture capable of supporting a wide range of single-qubit protocols.

Existing camera-to-robot pose estimation methods either rely on time-consuming iterative rendering, PnP based on predicted 2D keypoints with limited robustness or 3D registration which suffers from monocular scale ambiguity and complex training configuration. Moreover, we introduce Graph-guided Condition Generator (GCG), which generates condition for flow matching based on correlation among keypoints. Besides, we introduce Bone Length Loss and Ray-based Loss for decoupled training and scale consistency, with joint-wise weighting to mitigate varied prediction difficulty across joints. The proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art methods for pose estimation across different types of robots with multiple cameras, as well as for zero-shot cross-scene robot pose estimation. Although recent extensions enable temporal 3D prediction, their future evolution remains weakly conditioned on driving intentions and actions, limiting their ability to model alternative action-dependent futures. We propose \textbf{VGGTWorld-VLA}, an intention-conditioned extension of VGGT-World for controllable 3D world evolution in autonomous driving. First, we introduce an action--semantic conditioning mechanism that injects complementary driving semantics and ego-motion representations into the future-token stream, enabling different future geometry predictions for the same observed scene under alternative ego actions. Second, we develop a geometry--language--action bridge that adapts historical geometry, VLA semantic features, and maneuver and trajectory representations for joint conditioning of future geometry prediction. We evaluate future geometry prediction on NAVSIM, with ablation studies examining the contributions of semantic and action conditioning. Compared with baseline, our method reduces future-depth RMSE by 13.7\% and improves $\delta_1$ by 4.11 percentage points on NAVSIM motion subset. Controlled action-input interventions further show that the model uses the supplied action information. These results support semantic and action conditioning for controllable VGGT-based world prediction in autonomous driving.

In a recent development, arXiv:2605.02565v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recently, sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD) has emerged as a promising approach to compute ground and excited states of problem Hamiltonians. This method classically diagonalizes a Hamiltonian in a subspace that is spanned by samples obtained from a quantum computer. However, by its nature, SQD suffers from a fundamental sampling problem, as some basis states that are required for a targeted accuracy may only be sampled extremely rarely. To alleviate this limitation, we introduce the SQD-AA algorithm that combines SQD with amplitude amplification (AA). SQD-AA uses AA to sequentially reduce probabilities of already measured bitstrings, thus making the observation of new ones more likely. We observe a reduction in the total query complexity of more than a factor 100 for algebraically and exponentially decaying model distributions, and analytically show a quadratic advantage for the latter. Moreover, we evaluate real molecules in an early fault-tolerant scenario and compare SQD-AA to SQD and iterative quantum phase estimation (iQPE). For almost all considered examples, we observe the lowest total number of T-gates for SQD-AA while only requiring circuits that are 2-4 orders of magnitude shallower than those needed for iQPE. Given this substantial reduction in circuit depth compared to iQPE while saving 2 orders of magnitude in total runtime compared to SQD, we expect a significant regime in early fault-tolerance where SQD-AA runs feasibly, but iQPE circuits are too deep to execute confidently.

The diagnostic's rank test on 24 fresh checkpoints fails, so the association does not establish a predictive rule. Offline analyses show local benefits on some tasks and positive estimates for both proposal refitting and final selection. End-of-search polishing also helps, leaving the need for repeated refitting unresolved.

arXiv:2609.34982v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown great promise for robotic manipulation by mapping multi-modal semantics to physical actions. However, this mapping inherently struggles to align these coarse-grained semantics with fine-grained temporal execution. It leaves VLA models with limited generalization and insufficient robustness in cluttered environments. To overcome this issue, we propose ActionUNet, an efficient multi-scale fine-tuning framework that enhances pre-trained VLA models with minimal computational cost. ActionUNet first constructs a lightweight temporal U-Net within the temporal-aligned action feature space to fuse hierarchical structural priors, effectively bridging the scale gap between semantics and temporal executions. Recognizing that multi-scale modeling can disrupt microscopic temporal continuity and cause mechanical oscillations, ActionUNet then employs a conditional SIREN as a continuous action decoder. Equipped with explicit second-order smoothness constraints, this decoder guarantees temporal continuity and reduces high-frequency motion jitter. By smoothing temporal discontinuities from multi-scale fusion, this continuous formulation reduces mechanical execution failures while preserving the base VLA model's generalization and manipulation robustness. Extensive experiments on RoboTwin 2.0 and LIBERO-Plus benchmarks, together with real-world hard evaluations, demonstrate that ActionUNet significantly improves {\pi}0.5 success rates by absolute 9.8%, 6.1%, and 11.4%, respectively, while also generalizing to the regression-based OpenVLA-OFT backbone, highlighting its effectiveness and efficiency as a fine-tuning strategy. Code and implementation details are available at https://github.com/Di-Zhu123/ActionUNet.

Rollback the World, Keep the Reflection: Rollback-Induced Reflection for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (189 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

arXiv:2609.18304v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly tackle long-horizon tasks through multi-step environment interaction, yet a single erroneous action can alter subsequent states and observations, causing errors to compound over time. Existing methods either correct the context without repairing altered environment states or restore earlier states while discarding useful experience, making it difficult to both eliminate failure conditions and avoid repeating past mistakes. We argue that reliable recovery should instead be treated as a rollback-boundary control problem that jointly determines when to intervene, where to resume, and what information should survive recovery. Based on this view, we propose Rollback-Induced Reflection (RIR), a unified recovery framework that restores execution to a selected prior state while carrying forward reusable knowledge distilled from the abandoned trajectory to guide subsequent decisions. We further characterize recovery through a unified operator over rollback depth and retained memory, providing a general view of state restoration and knowledge retention. Experiments on three long-horizon benchmarks show that RIR consistently improves average task performance across multiple LLM backbones, with structured reflection memory preserving useful experience and selective rollback enabling efficient recovery.

In a recent development, arXiv:2604.01157v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate entanglement in and out of equilibrium in a one-dimensional Bose gas in its low-energy Bogoliubov regime. In this Gaussian setting, the state is fully characterized by its covariance matrix, which allows us to detect and quantify entanglement directly from the density and phase fluctuations of the gas. For thermal states, we determine the optimal entanglement witness arising from the covariance matrix criterion and show that it has a remarkably simple form: it depends only on the density fluctuations of the lowest normal mode and on the phase fluctuations of the highest one. For Dirichlet boundary conditions, this gives the exact temperature below which the gas is entangled, which, for many pixels, is given by $k_BT_{\rm sep}\simeq0.83\,\hbar c_0/\Delta$, where $c_0$ is the speed of sound and $\Delta$ the size of the pixels used to resolve the gas. We then study out-of-equilibrium dynamics induced by unitary compression and show that entanglement can be generated even from initially separable thermal states. This requires a non-adiabatic compression, since an adiabatic compression acts separately, and in the same way, on every pixel and therefore conserves entanglement. Moreover, the amount of entanglement created is limited by the compression ratio. We finally discuss how a subsequent contact with a thermal bath, modeled by global or local master equations, affects entanglement. Our methods and results provide a unified and physically intuitive picture of how entanglement emerges and evolves in 1D quantum Bose gases, and identify a simple optimal witness that is relevant more broadly to the analysis of entanglement in quadratic bosonic models and of its role in thermodynamic transformations.

Sources indicate that arXiv:2608.11229v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Preference learning is a powerful tool for reward learning, but treats the teacher as a passive oracle that answers queries driven by the learner. This learner-guided query selection ignores the teacher's knowledge of the solution. We reverse the typical preference query selection method by having the teacher create ordered preference pairs, since a teacher who knows the target can choose more informative pairs than a learner choosing its own queries. Exploiting this advantage requires the teacher to model what the learner knows, and that model goes stale when the learner's belief changes in ways the teacher cannot see, as when several teachers each teach without knowing what the others taught. We call this teacher-model drift. In this work, we use second-order Theory-of-Mind (ToM-2) to have the learner create understanding statements that correct the teacher's model of the learner's knowledge. In simulation, we show that a learner with a perfect teacher, one with perfect knowledge of the learner, needs about half as many rounds as learner-guided querying to learn the reward. Yet when teacher-model drift is induced by alternating between four co-teachers, the advantage erodes. We tested two types of understanding statement generation: the learner's mean belief and ToM-2 drift minimization. ToM-2 statements reduced the drift and recovered more of the lost advantage than mean statements. In a within-subjects study (n = 101) with a simulated ideal co-teacher, ToM-2 statements raised the learner's final alignment with the true reward above both uninformed and mean-informed teaching; on the regret participants removed in their own rounds, they outperformed uninformed teaching but not mean statements.

Sources indicate that arXiv:2603.29754v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Understanding how coherent driving and quantum dissipation cooperatively control nonequilibrium energy transfer is challenging in driven open quantum systems. Here, we develop a driven quantum master equation (dQME) that uses the eigenstates of the full driven Hamiltonian in the rotating frame and retains the driving phase in the system-reservoir interactions. This approach includes driving effects in both coherent evolution and dissipative exchange processes. We apply this approach to a coupled-qubit charger-battery system and dissipative energy transfer through one and two driven qubits. For a driven coupled-qubit battery, weak driving produces three peaks in stored energy near the central and two side resonances, whereas strong driving merges these peaks into a broad central peak. Ergotropy and charging efficiency are suppressed at the weak-driving resonances as battery coherence decreases. The central suppression of charging efficiency persists under strong driving. For dissipative energy transfer, the driven single-qubit model reveals three energy exchange channels set by the driving frequency and the dressed-state energy gap. Interqubit coupling produces additional current resonances, while strong driving broadens the frequency range of enhanced energy currents. We hope that the dQME may provide a common framework for understanding coherent energy charging and dissipative energy transfer.

Industry observers note that arXiv:2603.23036v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study zero-uncertainty states (ZUSs) for projective readout with quantum memory. In such tasks, Alice and Bob first share a quantum state. Alice then chooses one measurement from a prescribed family of projection-valued measures (PVMs), performs the measurement, and reveals her choice. Bob must infer Alice's outcome from his memory system with zero error. We prove that the admissible shared states are governed by the operator algebra generated by the entire PVM family, and in the physically important case where both systems have equal dimension and the measurements generate the full matrix algebra, every ZUS must be pure and maximally entangled. As a further application to quantum state verification, we use this purity result to give a direct proof that the target maximally entangled state is uniquely verified, extending Zhu's uniqueness criterion to degenerate projective measurements. Moreover, for protocols built from rank-one binary settings, we find an optimal spectral gap of $(3-\sqrt3)/6$ using three settings on two qutrits in $d=3$, and we also characterize all strategies attaining this gap. Finally, we show that different relaxations of exact readout yield inequivalent notions of approximate ZUSs depending on the task.

In a recent development, arXiv:2603.05137v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Classical shadows allow many properties of a quantum system to be estimated from relatively few measurements. Their standard guarantees, however, assume independent and identically distributed experimental rounds and a fixed analysis procedure. These assumptions can fail when the source drifts or the analysis adapts to previous measurement outcomes. We show that average expectation values along the run can be estimated with the usual classical-shadow sample-complexity scaling, even when the prepared states depend arbitrarily on the past and the analysis learns from earlier outcomes. For bounded shadow estimators, we further derive error bars that adapt to the observed data and remain valid throughout the experiment, allowing measurements to stop once the desired precision is reached. We illustrate these results numerically by certifying entanglement hidden by time averaging and reducing the measurements needed to estimate energy densities in many-body systems with small fluctuations.

arXiv:2602.06171v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum computing offers an alternative paradigm for addressing combinatorial optimization problems compared to classical methods. However, despite recent hardware improvements, the execution of empirical quantum optimization experiments at scales known to be hard for state-of-the-art classical solvers is not yet in reach. In this work, we offer a different way to approach combinatorial optimization with near-term quantum computing. Motivated by the promising results observed in using quantum-enhanced Markov chain Monte Carlo (QeMCMC) for approximating complicated probability distributions, we combine ideas of sampling from the device with QeMCMC together with warm-starting and parallel tempering, in the context of combinatorial optimization. We demonstrate empirically that our algorithm recovers the global optima for instances of the Maximum Independent Set problem (MIS) up to 117 decision variables using 117 qubits on IBM quantum hardware. We observe an indication of more favorable scaling relative to the tested classical MCMC methods on the chosen MIS instances. MIS is practically relevant across domains such as financial services and molecular biology. Although some MIS instances with a few hundred variables can be difficult for classical solvers, the instances studied here are solved efficiently by CPLEX.

It has been revealed that arXiv:2608.08049v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper presents a parameter-dependent linear matrix inequality (LMI) synthesis framework for trajectory tracking of nonholonomic mobile robots subject to multiplicative wheel slip. A sampled polytopic convex formulation jointly targets four design objectives on the variational dynamics in Kanayama coordinates: a prescribed exponential decay rate, an H-infinity disturbance-to-error gain, regional pole placement, and a weighted gain bound acting as a design-time actuator budget. The inverse metric and the auxiliary gain are parameterized affinely in the reference linear and angular velocities. A Slip-to-Disturbance Lemma provides an explicit closed-form upper bound on the additive disturbance equivalent to bounded multiplicative wheel slip in Kanayama coordinates, connecting the physical slip mechanism to the convex synthesis. The dissipation inequality is established at the sixteen vertices of the parameter-rate polytope, and a Lipschitz-based residual condition is given as a sufficient criterion for extending feasibility to interior points; the regions where the criterion succeeds for the synthesized controller, and where it does not, are both reported. An integral representation of the Kanayama residual lifts the variational certificate to a pointwise exponential-plus-ISS bound on the trajectory error directly from the LMI. The certified envelope is the semi-global ball at sigma_bar = 0.10; variable-terrain tests at slip ratios up to plus-minus 50% are reported as empirical observations outside that envelope. In the certified regime, the LPV controller and a fixed-gain LMI baseline produce quantitatively similar tracking records; on the severe-slip probes, the parameter-dependent design retains modest reproducible margins over both the fixed-gain and the classical Kanayama baselines.

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (223 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

arXiv:2607.27924v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In the physical world we inhabit, space and time are fundamentally continuous. However, existing machine learning paradigms for world modeling are largely confined to discrete-time prediction, thereby exhibiting significant inefficiency in capturing the dynamics of physical world. We introduce Physical-Time Flow (PT-Flow), a novel approach that learns a continuous latent velocity field operating in physical time. Crucially, the underlying dynamics of sequential data are parameterized by an ordinary differential equation (ODE) embedded in a well-structured representation space. Under this paradigm, the prediction of future can be recast as temporal integration via an ODE solver in the compressed latent space. Building upon PT-Flow, we construct ODEWorld, a continuous-time latent world model that is both efficient and versatile. By extracting time-variant features and enforcing ODE properties on both the dynamical representation space and the latent velocity field, ODEWorld effectively addresses the long-standing representation collapse concern in latent world model literature. This also enables high-quality image reconstruction even after long-horizon prediction. Moreover, its continuous nature allows for arbitrary temporal resolution and even backward prediction, which is impossible for most discrete-time models. Lastly, ODEWorld can provide rich planning-oriented information to facilitate downstream policy learning. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that ODEWorld successfully reconciles planning-conducive dynamics abstraction with visual realism, excelling in both video generation and robotic control. A three-stage state-current observer provides relative-velocity estimates to a nonlinear feedforward term for dominant current rejection and to an LMI-certified LPV-$\mathcal{H}_\infty$ correction layer. Feedback-linearising cancellation yields a constant input matrix, enabling convex synthesis without pairwise cross terms. A residual-level break-even law reveals that the effective surge disturbance depends on current-estimation error, while a singular-perturbation analysis proves local practical uniform ultimate boundedness on the embedded LPV model. REMUS simulations over three trajectories and four current scenarios show 89-96% current-estimation reduction, about 99% translational residual reduction, and RMS tracking-error reduction from 4.04 m to 0.24 m.
